response.answer: As an Admin, you generate progress reports for an exam after all marks have been entered [p. 24, p. 12]. The process involves several steps: first, the system calculates each student's total obtained marks, total maximum marks, and overall percentage for the exam [p. 12]. Next, a grade is assigned to each report based on the student's percentage and the defined grade scale [p. 12]. Subsequently, students are assigned a class rank based on their performance percentage [p. 12]. Finally, the progress reports are published, and subject-wise breakdowns are inserted into `progress_report_items` for students to view [p. 12].

citations.name: School Management Database - User Manual.pdf
citations.excerpt:
Generate reports for a new exam once all marks are entered (replace 2 with the exam_id
and 1 with the admin user_id):
INSERT INTO progress_reports (student_id, exam_id, total_max_marks, 
total_obtained, percentage, generated_by)
SELECT m.student_id, es.exam_id, SUM(es.max_marks), SUM(m.marks_obtained),
       ROUND(100 * SUM(m.marks_obtained) / SUM(es.max_marks), 2), 1
FROM marks m JOIN exam_schedules es ON es.exam_schedule_id = 
m.exam_schedule_id
WHERE es.exam_id = 2
GROUP BY m.student_id, es.exam_id;
UPDATE progress_reports pr
SET grade_id = (SELECT g.grade_id FROM grade_scale g WHERE pr.percentage 
BETWEEN g.min_percent AND g.max_percent)
WHERE pr.exam_id = 2;
UPDATE progress_reports pr SET class_rank = r.rk
FROM (SELECT report_id, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY percentage DESC) AS rk
      FROM progress_reports WHERE exam_id = 2) r
WHERE pr.report_id = r.report_id;
UPDATE progress_reports SET is_published = TRUE WHERE exam_id = 2;
Also insert the subject lines into progress_report_items  (one row per subject per
report) so students can see the subject-wise breakdown.

documentation.answer: The school's system identifies students with attendance percentages below 75% using the `v_student_attendance_report` view [p. 10, p. 19]. As an Admin, you can query this view to see total periods, attended periods, and the attendance percentage for each student, ordered by lowest percentage first [p. 9, p. 19]. However, the provided documentation does not specify the school's policies or guidelines regarding actions to be taken for low student attendance once identified.

citations.name: School Management Database - User Manual.pdf
citations.excerpt:
Students below 75 percent:
SELECT * FROM v_student_attendance_report WHERE attendance_pct < 75;
Attendance for one section on one date:
SELECT u.first_name, u.last_name, p.period_no, sub.subject_name, sa.status
FROM student_attendance sa
JOIN students s ON s.student_id = sa.student_id
JOIN users u ON u.user_id = s.user_id
JOIN periods p ON p.period_id = sa.period_id
JOIN subjects sub ON sub.subject_id = sa.subject_id
WHERE s.section_id = 2 AND sa.attendance_date = '2026-11-02'
ORDER BY u.first_name, p.period_no;
Faculty attendance summary:
SELECT f.employee_no, u.first_name, u.last_name, fa.status, COUNT(*) AS days
FROM faculty_attendance fa
JOIN faculty f ON f.faculty_id = fa.faculty_id
JOIN users u ON u.user_id = f.user_id
GROUP BY f.employee_no, u.first_name, u.last_name, fa.status
ORDER BY f.employee_no;
6.5 Leave approvals
See pending requests from students and faculty:
SELECT * FROM v_pending_leaves;
Approve or reject (the admin user_id goes in reviewed_by ):
UPDATE leave_requests
SET status = 'Approved', reviewed_by = 1, reviewed_on = NOW(), admin_remarks 
= 'Approved. Get well soon.'
WHERE leave_id = 2;
Use status Rejected  and a remark to reject a request.

6.4 Build the timetable
Insert one row per period. The database blocks clashes automatically: a section, a teacher
or a room cannot be used twice in the same period on the same day.
INSERT INTO timetable (section_id, day_of_week, period_id, subject_id, 
faculty_id, classroom_id)
VALUES (2, 'Tuesday', 1, 1, 1, 2);
View the timetable of one section:
SELECT day_of_week, period_no, start_time, subject_name, faculty_name, 
room_name
FROM v_timetable
WHERE section = 'Grade 10-A'
ORDER BY CASE day_of_week WHEN 'Monday' THEN 1 WHEN 'Tuesday' THEN 2 WHEN 
'Wednesday' THEN 3
  WHEN 'Thursday' THEN 4 WHEN 'Friday' THEN 5 ELSE 6 END, period_no;

Student attendance percentage for everyone, lowest first:
